fields.label: Distributor
fields.description: Who is out of pocket. He gave the discount or the stock at the counter the moment a rep promised it, and this document is how he gets it back.

fields.label: Customer
fields.description: The distributor party in our books, which is who the credit note is raised against. Read-only and resolved from the profile, because a claim settled to the wrong ledger is worse than one not settled at all.

fields.label: Status
fields.options:
Draft
Pending Approval
Approved
Settled
Rejected
Cancelled
fields.description: Approval and settlement are two events weeks apart, so they are two states. Approved means we agree we owe it; Settled means a credit note exists and the money has moved. Collapsing them would leave a distributor unable to tell an agreed claim from a paid one, which is the single thing he opens this screen to find out.

fields.label: From
fields.description: Matched against the ledger posting_date - the day the benefit was granted at the counter - and never against the day a phone finally got signal.

fields.label: Scheme
fields.description: Set where the distributor claims one scheme on its own, which is how a principal usually wants them. Blank means every scheme that ran in the window.

fields.label: Distributor Reference
fields.description: The number the distributor files this under at his end. He will quote it on the phone, and without it here nobody at our end can find the document he is talking about.

fields.label: Bill Discounts
fields.description: What came off shop bills. Kept apart from free-goods value because the two are settled differently and argued about separately.

fields.label: Approved
fields.description: What we agree to pay, which is not always what was claimed. The credit note is raised for this figure, never for the claimed one.

fields.label: Eligible Ledger Rows
fields.description: How many accruals the window actually holds for this distributor, counted from the ledger at save time rather than from the lines attached.

fields.label: Reconciles
fields.description: Set only where the lines attached come to the same paise as the accruals the window holds. A claim that does not reconcile is still allowed to exist, because a distributor may deliberately claim part of a month, but it is flagged: an unflagged partial claim and an unflagged missing accrual look identical at approval.

fields.label: Rejection Reason
fields.description: A rejection with no reason written down generates a phone call every single time.

fields.label: Credit Note
fields.description: The return invoice raised against the distributor Customer. This is the only accounting document a claim ever produces, and it is raised on approval, never on submission.

fields.label: Settlement Reference
fields.description: Where the credit landed, usually the primary invoice it was adjusted against. It is what the accountant at the other end looks for and nothing else.
